Rashi on Pesachim 58b:10:1.hebrew: כל השנים - שערב הפסח חל בחול, דשחטינהו בשבע ומחצה. ור"ע אמר: כסידרו ערב הפסח שחל להיות בערב שבת:
Rashi on Pesachim 58b:10:1.english: All years - when Passover eve falls on a weekday, when we slaughter them at seven and a half [hours]. And Rabbi Akiva says: in accordance with its arrangement on Passover eve that occurs on Shabbat eve.

Rashi on Pesachim 58b:11:1.hebrew: מניין שלא יהא דבר - נקטר במערכה משנערכה שחרית, קודם לתמיד של שחר. ת"ל וערך עליה, בתר ובער עליה הכהן כתיב, דהוא סידור מערכה:
Rashi on Pesachim 58b:11:1.english: From where [is it derived] that nothing - [that is] burned on the wood-pile once it has been arranged in the morning [shall] precede the daily morning offering? The verse states: "and he shall arrange upon it" — [this] is written after "and the priest shall kindle upon it," which is the arrangement of the wood-pile.

Rashi on Pesachim 58b:11:2.english: What is the derivation - [how is it derived] that this [term] "the burnt-offering" refers to the daily morning offering?

Rashi on Pesachim 58b:11:3.hebrew: העולה עולה ראשונה - מדלא כתיב וערך עליה עולה אלא העולה, הכי קאמר: וערך עליה מיד העולה החשובה האמורה תחלה לכל העולות. והיינו עולת תמיד דפרשת קרבנות [בפ' פינחס], דקרבן תמיד כתיב ברישא:
Rashi on Pesachim 58b:11:3.english: "The burnt-offering" — the first burnt-offering - Since it is not written "and he shall arrange upon it a burnt-offering," rather "the burnt-offering," this is what [the verse] is saying: and he shall arrange upon it immediately the prominent burnt-offering, which is stated first of all the burnt-offerings; and this is the daily burnt-offering of the section of sacrifices [in Parashat Pinchas], for the daily offering is written first.

Rashi on Pesachim 58b:12:1.hebrew: והקטיר עליה - אתמיד קאי, דסיפיה דקרא הוא, וה"ק: והקטיר על העולה הזאת — כלומר אחריה — חלבי השלמים:
Rashi on Pesachim 58b:12:1.english: And [he] shall cause to go up in smoke upon it - It refers to the daily [morning] offering, for [this] is the end of the verse, and this is what it is saying: "And [he] shall cause to go up in smoke upon this burnt-offering" — that is to say, after it — "the fats of the peace-offerings."

Rashi on Pesachim 58b:13:1.english: And say [that] it is peace-offerings that are not offered - after the daily afternoon offering.

Rashi on Pesachim 58b:14:1.english: The daily offering - [That] of the afternoon precedes the Paschal lamb.

Rashi on Pesachim 58b:14:2.hebrew: לקטורת - של בין הערבים, וכולהו יליף טעמא:
Rashi on Pesachim 58b:14:2.english: [Before] the incense - Of the afternoon, and [the Gemara] derives the reason for all of them.

Rashi on Pesachim 58b:14:3.english: To the lamps - [This refers] to the lighting of the lamps.

Rashi on Pesachim 58b:1:1.hebrew: אי לא חייש ניעבדיה בשש ומחצה - דהא הפסחים מרובין, ובשבת לא בעי לאיחוריה משום נדרים ונדבות:
Rashi on Pesachim 58b:1:1.english: If he is not concerned, let us sacrifice it at six and a half [hours] - For the Paschal lambs are numerous, and on Shabbat one does not need to delay it because of vow and free-will offerings.

Rashi on Pesachim 58b:1:2.hebrew: קסבר מוספין קודמין לבזיכין - ועל כרחך בזיכין בשבע, ואינן פנויין בה:
Rashi on Pesachim 58b:1:2.english: He holds: The additional offerings precede the bowls - And perforce the bowls [are offered] at seven [hours], and they are not free during [that hour].

Rashi on Pesachim 58b:3:1.english: Ordinarily - All the days of the week, at eight and a half [hours].

Rashi on Pesachim 58b:3:2.hebrew: כך סידרו - בשבתות של כל השנה. ואף על גב דליכא נדרים ונדבות, חיישינן לסרך נדרים דחול, דילמא אתו למיסרך ולמיעבד בחול נמי בשבע, ומיפסלי נדרים ונדבות של אחריו:
Rashi on Pesachim 58b:3:2.english: So is its arrangement - On the Shabbatot of the entire year. And even though there are no vow-offerings or freewill-offerings [on Shabbat], we are concerned about a carryover to weekday vow-offerings, lest they come to follow the habit and do [it] on a weekday as well at seven [hours], and the vow-offerings and freewill-offerings [brought] after it would be disqualified.

Rashi on Pesachim 58b:4:1.hebrew: ר"ע אומר - כל שבתות השנה הוא נשחט בשבע ומחצה, כסידרו ערב הפסח, דלא גזרינן משום חול:
Rashi on Pesachim 58b:4:1.english: Rabbi Akiva says - [On] all Shabbats of the year, it is slaughtered at seven and a half [hours], like its arrangement [on] Passover eve, for we do not decree on account of a weekday.

Rashi on Pesachim 58b:4:2.hebrew: דברי הכל היא - דר' ישמעאל ורבי עקיבא לא איירי בערב פסח כלל, וכמתניתין סבירא להו בין בחול בין בשבת:
Rashi on Pesachim 58b:4:2.english: It is the opinion of all - For Rabbi Yishmael and Rabbi Akiva are not speaking of Passover eve at all, and they hold like our Mishnah, whether on a weekday or on Shabbat.

Rashi on Pesachim 58b:6:1.english: Let us sacrifice it at six and a half [hours] - For the zealous are early to [perform] mitzvot.

Rashi on Pesachim 58b:6:2.english: [He] holds [that] the additional offerings precede the bowls [of frankincense] - This is our reading.

Rashi on Pesachim 58b:7:1.english: Like [when] it occurs on Monday - [on] the eve of Passover, when the daily offering is slaughtered at seven and a half [hours].

Rashi on Pesachim 58b:7:2.hebrew: בשני בשבת - חד מימות החול נקט. ואית דאמרי: יומא קמא דשבתא דחזי לארביסר נקט, וחד בשבתא לא חזי לארביסר, דלא בד"ו פסח. ולאו מילתא היא, שהרי על פי הראייה היו מקדשין:
Rashi on Pesachim 58b:7:2.english: On a Monday - [The baraita] mentioned one of the weekdays [as an example]. And some say: it mentioned the first day of the week that is fit for the fourteenth [of Nisan], as Sunday is not fit for the fourteenth, since Passover [cannot fall on] Monday, Wednesday, or Friday. But this is not [a valid point], for they used to sanctify [the new month] based on sighting [the new moon].

Rashi on Pesachim 58b:7:3.hebrew: ור"ע אומר כסידרו ערב הפסח - גרסינן, ותו לא:
Rashi on Pesachim 58b:7:3.english: And Rabbi Akiva says: like its arrangement on the eve of Passover - We read [this], and nothing more.

Rashi on Pesachim 58b:8:1.hebrew: בשלמא לאביי ניחא - דמדקאמר רבי ישמעאל "חל להיות בשבת כחל להיות בשני בשבת", על כרחך "כסידרו ערב הפסח" דקאמר ר"ע, בע"פ שחל להיות בע"ש קאמר:
Rashi on Pesachim 58b:8:1.english: Granted, according to Abaye, [it] works out well - For since Rabbi Yishmael says, "[If it] occurs on Shabbat, [it is] as [if it] occurred on a Monday," perforce "like its arrangement [on] the eve of Passover" that Rabbi Akiva says refers to the eve of Passover that occurs on the eve of Shabbat.

Rashi on Pesachim 58b:8:2.hebrew: אלא לרבא - דקאמר רבי ישמעאל למיכמר בישרא חייש, וכסידרו בחול בעלמא קאמר, הא קתני הכא: כחל להיות בשני בשבת:
Rashi on Pesachim 58b:8:2.english: But according to Rava - who says [that] Rabbi Yishmael is concerned about the meat spoiling, and means [that it is offered] in its regular order on an ordinary weekday — surely it teaches here: "[It is] as if it occurred on a Monday."

Rashi on Pesachim 58b:8:3.hebrew: אלא אימא כשני בשבת - שאינו ערב הפסח, דהיינו בשמונה ומחצה, דחיישינן למיכמר בישרא:
Rashi on Pesachim 58b:8:3.english: Rather say: Like a Monday - [an ordinary Monday] that is not the eve of Passover, which is at eight and a half [hours], for we are concerned about the meat spoiling.

Rashi on Pesachim 58b:9:1.hebrew: כסדר כל השנה - היינו בשמונה ומחצה, דחיישי' למיכמר בישרא:
Rashi on Pesachim 58b:9:1.english: In accordance with the arrangement of the entire year - That is, at eight and a half [hours], for we are concerned about the meat becoming heated [and spoiling].

Tosafot on Pesachim 58b:11:1.hebrew: העולה עולה ראשונה - תימה, דבזבחים פ' כל התדיר (זבחים דף פט.) מפקינן מקרא אחרינא, דתנן: "התמידין קודמין למוספין, שנאמר: 'מלבד עולת הבקר אשר לעולת התמיד'". וליכא למימר דהתם איצטריך לצבור שאין להן תמידין ומוספין אלא כדי אחד מהם, דהא קתני התם: "דם חטאת קודם לדם עולה", ודומיא דזה הוי תמידין ומוספין. וליכא למימר נמי דאיצטריך קרא תנינא לעכב, דבהתכלת (מנחת דף מט:) אמרינן בהדיא דליכא עיכובא. וי"ל, דהתם איצטריך למוספין דלא קדמי, והכא לנדרים ונדבות; וצריכי, דשמא מוספין חמירי שהן קרבן צבור, או שמא נדרים ונדבות חמירי שרגילים ומצויים יותר. אי נמי: קרא דהכא להקדמת הקטרה, דבהקטרה כתיב: "וערך עליה העולה", וקרא דכל התדיר להקדמת שחיטה, ד"תעשו את אלה" בעשיית הדם כתיב. והא דפריך בהתכלת (שם) גבי הא דתנן: "התמידין אין מעכבין את המוספין", וקאמר: "היכי דמי? אילימא דאית ליה ולקדם — והתניא: מנין שלא יהא דבר כו'", ומייתי הא דרבא ולא מייתי קרא ד"מלבד" — משום דלשון "שלא יהא דבר קודם" משמע טפי עיכוב; [להכי] אתייה טפי מן המשנה. אי נמי: למימרא דאפי' בהקטרה, דלא תנן בכל התדיר, תמיד של שחר קודם. אך קשה: דאמאי איצטריך "העולה" ו"מלבד"? תיפוק לי' דתמיד קודם למוספין, דבתמיד כתיב "בבקר", ובמוספין כתיב "ביום", דמשמע בעיצומו של יום! ולמאי דאמרי' בהתכלת דליכא עיכובא בהקדמה לתמיד, אתי שפיר הא דאמרינן בריש עירובין (דף ב.): "שלמים ששחטן קודם פתיחת דלתות ההיכל פסולים, שנאמר: 'ושחטו פתח אהל מועד' — בזמן שהן פתוחין ולא בזמן שהן נעולין", דמטעם ששחטן קודם תמיד של שחר לא הוו פסולין. והא דתני בתוספתא דמכילתין [פ"ד]: "כל הקדשים שהקריבן קודם תמיד של שחר או שעיכבן אחר תמיד של בין הערבים פסולין, שאין לך קודם לתמיד של שחר אלא קטורת, ואין לך שמתעכב אחר תמיד של בין הערבים כו'" — האי "פסולין" היינו מדרבנן. [ועיין תוס' עירובין ב'. ד"ה שלמים, ותוס' יומא כט. ד"ה אלא, ע"ש היטב שכתבו להדיא, אבל לשון התוספתא משמע דאפי' זרק הדם בדיעבד ועשה כל מצות אפ"ה פסולין, דקתני "שהקריבו" ולא קתני "ששחטן"; ואי מדרבנן, אמאי פסולין וכו'.]:
Tosafot on Pesachim 58b:11:1.english: "The burnt-offering" — the first burnt-offering - This is surprising, for in Zevachim, chapter Kol HaTadir (89a), we derive [this] from a different verse, as we learned in a Mishnah: "The daily offerings precede the musaf offerings, as it is stated: 'Aside from the burnt-offering of the morning, which is for the continual burnt-offering.'" And one cannot say that there it is needed [only] for a congregation that does not have [enough for both] daily offerings and musaf offerings, but only enough for one of them, for it teaches there: "The blood of a sin-offering precedes the blood of a burnt-offering," and similar to this is [the case of] daily offerings and musaf offerings. Nor can one say that a second verse is needed to make it indispensable, for in [chapter] HaTechelet (Menachot 49b) we say explicitly that there is no indispensability. And one can say that there it is needed for musaf offerings, that they should not precede [the daily offering], whereas here it is for vowed and freewill offerings; and both are needed, for perhaps musaf offerings are more stringent since they are communal offerings, or perhaps vowed and freewill offerings are more stringent since they are more frequent and common. Alternatively: the verse here is for precedence in burning [on the altar], for regarding burning it is written, "And he shall arrange the burnt-offering upon it," whereas the verse in Kol HaTadir is for precedence in slaughter, for "you shall offer these" is written regarding the blood service. And as for that which [the Gemara] asks in HaTechelet (ibid.) regarding what we learned in the Mishnah: "The daily offerings do not prevent [the offering of] the musaf offerings," and it says: "What is the case? If we say that he has [both] and [the musaf] is to precede — was it not taught in a baraita: 'From where [is it derived] that nothing [shall precede...],' etc.," and it cites this [teaching] of Rava and does not cite the verse "Aside from" — [that is] because the wording "that nothing shall precede" implies indispensability more strongly; [therefore] it cited it rather than the Mishnah. Alternatively: to say that even in burning [on the altar], which was not taught in Kol HaTadir, the daily morning offering precedes. However, this is difficult: why are "the burnt-offering" and "aside from" needed? Let it be derived that the daily offering precedes the musaf offerings from the fact that regarding the daily offering it is written "in the morning," whereas regarding the musaf offerings it is written "on the day," which implies in the middle of the day! And according to what we say in HaTechelet that there is no indispensability regarding precedence to the daily offering, that which we say at the beginning of Eruvin (2a) fits well: "Peace-offerings that one slaughtered before the opening of the Sanctuary doors are invalid, as it is stated: 'And he shall slaughter it at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting' — when they are open and not when they are locked" — for on account of having slaughtered them before the daily morning offering they would not be invalid. And as for that which is taught in the Tosefta of our tractate [ch. 4]: "All sacrifices that one offered before the daily morning offering or delayed until after the daily afternoon offering are invalid, for you have nothing that precedes the daily morning offering except the incense, and you have nothing that is delayed after the daily afternoon offering, etc." — this [term] "invalid" is by rabbinic decree. [And see Tosafot on Eruvin 2a, s.v. Shelamim, and Tosafot on Yoma 29a, s.v. Ella; look closely there, for they wrote explicitly, though the wording of the Tosefta implies that even if one sprinkled the blood ex post facto and performed all the precepts, even so they are invalid, for it teaches "that they offered" and does not teach "that they slaughtered"; and if [it is] rabbinic, why are they invalid? etc.]

Tosafot on Pesachim 58b:4:1.hebrew: דברי הכל היא - ובין בחול ובין בשבת דקתני במתני' — לא קאי ארישא אלא אערב הפסח. והא דקאמר דברי הכל היא, היינו כלומר דמצינו למימר דברי הכל לפלוגתא דהך ברייתא דקיימינן עלה; אבל איכא שני ברייתות דמייתי בסמוך דפליגי בהדיא בשבת דערב פסח, ומהנהו ודאי איכא למיפשט דלאו דברי הכל היא:
Tosafot on Pesachim 58b:4:1.english: It is [in accordance with] all opinions - And [the phrase] "whether on a weekday or on Shabbat" that the Mishnah teaches does not refer to the first clause, but rather to Passover eve. And that which [the Gemara] says, "it is [in accordance with] all opinions," means to say that we can say [it is in accordance with] all opinions with respect to the dispute of this baraita that we are currently discussing; however, there are two baraitot that [the Gemara] cites shortly [below] that explicitly disagree regarding a Shabbat of Passover eve, and from those it can certainly be resolved that it is not [in accordance with] all opinions.

Tosafot on Pesachim 58b:4:2.hebrew: כאילו חל בשני בשבת - אין צריך לפרש דדוקא נקט שני, דהוא יומא קמא דמיקלע ביה ארבעה עשר, דחד בשבתא לא חזי לארביסר דלא בד"ו פסח; דהא ע"כ לרבא, דמוקי לה בשני בשבת דעלמא, לא הוי שני בשבת דוקא, דהא לא בערב הפסח מיירי — הוא הדין לאביי, אם לא יהיה דוקא אין לחוש. ורש"י שהקשה דעל פי הראייה היו מקדשין, אין נראה לר"י; דאע"ג דהיו מקדשין על פי הראייה, היו נזהרין שלא יבאו תרי שבי בהדי הדדי, דאמרינן בהדיא פרק קמא דראש השנה (דף כ.): "מאיימין על העדים על החדש שנראה בזמנו לומר שלא ראו". והא דאמרי' בשילהי אלו קשרים (שבת דף קיג.): "חלבי שבת קריבים ביום הכפורים", אלמא בהדי הדדי נינהו — מוקי לה בהחליל (סוכה דף נד:) כאחרים, דאמרי: אין בין עצרת לעצרת אלא ד' ימים בלבד:
Tosafot on Pesachim 58b:4:2.english: As if it occurred on Monday [lit. the second day of the week] - There is no need to explain that [the baraita] specifically chose Monday because it is the first day [of the week] on which the fourteenth [of Nisan] can fall, since Sunday is not fit for the fourteenth because Passover [does not fall on] Monday, Wednesday, or Friday [lo BeDU Pesach]; for perforce according to Rava, who establishes it as referring to an ordinary Monday, Monday is not [meant] specifically, since it is not speaking of Passover eve — [and] the same applies to Abaye: if it is not specific, there is nothing to be concerned about. And [as for] Rashi, who objected that they used to sanctify [the new month] based on sighting [the moon] — this does not appear [correct] to the Ri; for even though they sanctified [the month] based on sighting, they were careful that two Sabbaths [i.e., Shabbat and Yom Kippur] should not come adjacent to one another, as we say explicitly in the first chapter of Rosh Hashanah (20a): "They intimidate the witnesses regarding the new moon that was seen in its [proper] time, to tell them [to say] that they did not see [it]." And [as for] that which we say at the end of [the chapter] Eilu Kesharim (Shabbat 113a): "The fats of Shabbat may be offered on Yom Kippur," which implies that they are adjacent to one another — [the Gemara] in [the chapter] Hechalil (Sukkah 54b) establishes it as [following the view of] Acherim, who say: There are only four days between [one] Atzeret [Shavuot] and [the next] Atzeret:

Tosafot on Pesachim 58b:8:1.hebrew: אלא לרבא קשיא - תימה: לרבה בר עולא נמי תיקשי, דלדבריו לרבי עקיבא מוספין קודמין לבזיכין, ולפי מה שהברייתא כאביי לרבי עקיבא תמיד נשחט בשש ומחצה, וא"כ בזיכין קודמין למוספין. ותירץ רשב"א, דלרבה בר עולא לא קאי ר"ע אלא ארישא דקתני "תמיד כל השנה קרב כהלכתו" — משמע ל"ש חול ולא שנא שבת — ועלה פליג ר"ע ואמר דשבת דעלמא כערב הפסח, והיינו ממש כרבה בר עולא; או יתרץ כרבא:
Tosafot on Pesachim 58b:8:1.english: But according to Rava, it is difficult - It is astonishing: according to Rabbah bar Ulla as well it should be difficult, for according to his view, according to Rabbi Akiva, the musaf offerings precede the frankincense bowls, whereas according to how the baraita [reads] according to Abaye, according to Rabbi Akiva the daily offering is slaughtered at six and a half [hours], and if so, the frankincense bowls precede the musaf offerings. And Rashba answered that according to Rabbah bar Ulla, Rabbi Akiva is referring only to the first clause, which teaches, "The daily offering is sacrificed throughout the entire year in accordance with its law" — implying [that there is] no difference [whether it is] a weekday and no difference [whether it is] Shabbat — and regarding that [clause] Rabbi Akiva disagrees and says that an ordinary Shabbat is like the eve of Passover, and this is precisely like Rabbah bar Ulla; or else he can answer like Rava.
